He has come to ask permission to formally court Merlin: son of Balinor, Chief Dragonlord of Albion, and Hunith, Ygraine’s trusted lady-in-waiting. It should be simple. It is not. Because Merlin is not only the man Arthur loves. He is Dragonkind’s future, Dafyd’s blood, Druid-touched magic, and a sovereignty older than Pendragon law. As Arthur and Merlin’s courtship becomes public, Ascetir’s roots begin to stir, Dafyd’s tidal arches hum at the wrong tide, Avalon’s mists remember what Camelot forgot, and old roads bend toward the Forest of Balor and the Great Stones of Nemeton. But the second he starts winning, the skateboarding world becomes obsessed with him just as quickly as it once became obsessed with Arthur.And just like that, skateboarding’s biggest rivalry is born.Their rivalry is wheels grinding against concrete, sparks flying every time they share a park.Arthur calls Merlin reckless.Merlin calls Arthur predictable.Commentators frame them as control vs chaos, king vs sorcerer. But behind broken skateparks and after-hours sessions, something shifts between them.Trash talk turns quieter. Challenges become dares. Arguments end too close.
